changes.evidence: The enlarged glyph has a low, compressed m body and a separate, continuous shallow curved bar. The upper stroke has no return or enclosed eye establishing a raised e. The abbreviation is kept rather than expanded.
A detached dot belongs to the i; no two-sided circumflex is visible above the vowel. The a-r-a-i-t sequence is live.

changes.evidence: After clair there is a low horizontal dash followed by the raised opening quotation strokes and the separate i/l strokes. There is no q descender or u forming a preceding qu'.

changes.evidence: Two raised opening strokes stand before il at the end of the first line. The next line begins directly with suivre, without an opening pair there. Two raised closing strokes follow nez, before the three low ellipsis points. Both sides of the physical line break are located.
The q descender is followed by the low u/e trace, then a separate gap and the beginning of une. No apostrophe connects these two visibly separated words.

The upper addition shows initial e, two low s shoulders, a, the long oblique y descender, a, n, and a crossed final t, followed by d and a high apostrophe. A lead-in descends to the place after en and before écri. The word essayant is readable without a doubt mark.

Several dark cancellation strokes pass through the ending. An initial low down/up movement and a final tall crossed stroke support vant, but the interior a/n strokes cannot be isolated securely. Deletion is certain; the underlying letter reading remains uncertain.

changes.location: Possible live replacement ending of écri-
changes.h: No replacement ending in the body; note says the cancelled ending was not rewritten.
changes.evidence: A small rising/returning trace can be separated within the dark cancellation, but it is not securely distinguishable from the cancelling pen movement. The tentative re is retained as a presence-and-reading doubt; no separate clean replacement stands after the struck ending. An unreplaced écri- remains an alternative in the doubt record.
The initial C has a full-height open curved stroke immediately after the parenthesis; the following letters are lower. The capital is present.

changes.location: Two marks in the gap after Comme
changes.evidence: Two dark isolated points occur between Comme and une, one higher and left of the other. They are substantially darker than the surrounding paper streaks but are oblique rather than neatly vertical. A colon is a possible reading; intentional punctuation cannot be distinguished securely from incidental marks. Both witnesses omit them.
A rounded o has its own visible track, followed by a separately shaped low e and the u/x ending. The scan does not show a fused œ ligature.

A long q-like descender and a high apostrophe-like point survive beneath the replacement strokes. They support an earlier qu'on, but the superposition prevents securely partitioning all its letters or determining how much of the final on was reused. The earlier whole reading is retained only under a doubt mark.

Above the earlier q-like descender there is a tall looped d; the following small o/n joins lead to a distinctly crossed t. A separate round o and low n then give on. These live strokes settle dont on despite the surviving underlying trace.

changes.location: End of the parenthetical list, etc
changes.evidence: After the final c, the next visible stroke is the closing parenthesis. No separate point is visible in that gap.

changes.h: No earlier word in the body; note describes the next word as overwritten.
changes.evidence: A second long downward trace at the left and low looped remnants beyond the live u/i belong to superposed writing. They allow pour but do not expose a secure independent p-o-u-r sequence. The old reading remains tentative and is not inferred from the subsequent syntax.

The upper writing has a closed q bowl and descender, a raised u shoulder, and a separate dot for the final i. The additional low trace belongs to the underlying writing. The live word is readable as qui.

changes.location: Comma adjacent to the overwritten qui
changes.evidence: A distinct curved comma descends after the overwritten word and before soit. The gap between poussée and the overwritten word has no corresponding comma. The punctuation is therefore after qui.

The d/o/n/n sequence and a raised terminal e-like return are visible. The following dark, thickened tail curls downward and may be merely the e exit stroke; it is too dense to exclude an additional reduced r. Donne is preferred, with donner retained as a visual alternative.

changes.location: End of the first paragraph, type souhaité
changes.evidence: The word ends with a crossed t followed by one accented e and then a distinct period. There is no second final e between that accented letter and the period.
Each side of strictes has a pair of short raised strokes. No angular guillemet pair is drawn. The difference concerns the visible quotation shape, not the TeX wrapper.

After qu' the pronoun shows a short i stroke, one tall looped l, and the small terminal s. It does not contain the two tall l strokes and additional e body needed for elles. The following forment crosses the physical line break, but the pronoun itself does not.

changes.location: Near the foot, complexes de chaines
changes.evidence: A detached point is visible over i; no paired sloping circumflex strokes appear. The ending n/e/s is live and unstruck.

notes: Author content: the first paragraph continues an earlier discussion. It asks for a functor from ens. (semi) simpliciaux to n-groupoïdes and calls the associated geometric intuition very clear. No functor formula or arrow is drawn on this sheet.

Author proposal: a sufficiently complete and explicit Christmas wish-list of notions and their relations might lead to an axiomatic description, either enabling an explicit ad-hoc construction or permitting an existence-and-uniqueness theorem. The page does not supply such a construction or proof.

Author qualifiers and questions are preserved: me semblerait canularesque, Peut-être, voudrait disposer, arriverait-on, à la rigueur, n'ayant pas compris, je ne vois pas comment, mais peu importe, and D'accord ?. These are the author's expressed attitudes or uncertainties, not reader verdicts.

Author content: Segal's idea in the recipient's last letter was not understood; the author says that letter was sent to Illusie. The strict Picard n-category passage states a requested (n+1)-category and an (n+1)-equivalence to complexes of length n. This is a desideratum, not a theorem verified here.

Mathematical notation inspection: each n-cat. occurrence, each independent n+1 expression, both pairs of brackets, plus signs, the final length n and the interlinear placement were inspected. All are carried literally. No mathematical expectation was used to fill a glyph.

The revision after poussée yields the visibly irregular live order qui, soit donne/donner ... soit qui permette. It is preserved with the uncertain terminal verb reading and the definite insertion qui permette, rather than syntactically repaired.
The ordinary return strokes below rigueur, Segal and longueur are connected g descenders; no independent underline was transcribed.

The author page number is 2 and the archive foliation is 147. H's page label 146 is editorial metadata; its note already records the two visible numbers. There is no date, salutation, signature, printed heading, stamp, drawing or mathematical display on this sheet.
The first paragraph and the page ending are continuations. No preceding or following page was consulted. Je te remercie has no terminal period on the visible page.
Reader checks: this work was a full visual transcription and comparison. No proof, counterexample, recalculation or other mathematical check event was performed; checks is intentionally empty.

The prescribed crop.py was used once for each of six unresolved places, with 2800-pixel target width and its image-processing pipeline. Two slightly sloping loci were rotated by 2 degrees. No whole-page or half image was viewed again, and no OCR was used.

Residual uncertainty at re includes the possibility that all apparent replacement strokes are cancelling strokes. Residual uncertainty at the two points after Comme includes the possibility that neither is intentional punctuation. These uncertainties concern presence as well as reading.

coverage: The whole scan was viewed once for layout, then half a once and half b once in that order. All 27 physical body lines, including C/H agreements, were read against both complete witnesses. The inspection included the opening abbreviation; all accents and missing accents; abbreviation points, commas, ellipses and quotation shapes; word endings; every inline numeral, n, bracket, plus and dash; and each visible deletion, overwrite and interlinear addition. All margins and the author and archive numbers were inspected. There are two body paragraphs and no displays, diagrams or drawings. Six tight crops addressed only places left unresolved by the halves. Both source boxes are provided for the quoted line break, relations/notions revision, description, forment and the inline equivalence phrase. Neither witness omitted an independent body block. H does not transcribe the tentative underlying words after notions and poussée; its note explicitly discusses the incomplete écri revision. Two punctuation-like points after Comme are omitted by both witnesses and are retained with uncertain intentional status. All eight C doubt loci have resolution entries: the initial bar, live dont on and live qui are resolved; vant, possible re, underlying qu'on, underlying pour and donne/donner remain doubtful. The separate H doubt on essayant is resolved. The full page appears in reading.tex, with archive 147 only as a comment.
